english.title: Fail to produce / deliver rail ticket on request / give name and address
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a passenger by railway, failed, on request by an officer or servant of the railway company, to produce and deliver up a ticket showing that your fare was paid or to pay the fare from the place whence your journey started or to give your name and address
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(1) of the Regulation of Railways Act 1889.

english.notes:
(i) ALL of the 'components' of this offence are required before this offence is complete, i.e. there must be a request and failure to deliver up the ticket, failure to pay for a ticket and a failure to provided a name and address.
(ii) Section 5(2) authorises an employee of the company to detain a person who has failed to comply with section 5(1) until he or she "can be conveniently brought before some Justice or otherwise discharged by due course of law."
(iii) Police officers attending an incident where such a detention has occurred must satisfy themselves before making any arrest that the Necessity Test in section 24 of The Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 applies. Otherwise the detained person must be released and consideration given to reporting any offence which may have been committed.
(iv) If no intent to avoid the fare can be proved, the person may be dealt with under this subsection. If intent can be proved, consider either section 5(3)(a) or 5(3)(b) of the Regulation of Railways Act 1889, which relate to offences of travelling on the railway without paying the fare and proceeding beyond the distance of fare paid respectively.
